PyInstanceMethod_New.evidence: NO standalone out-of-line copy. In the stock reference _PyInstanceMethod_New (0x1f95c) has EXACTLY ONE caller: instancemethod_new (the type's tp_new). Under LTO the engine inlined its whole body into instancemethod_new (tp_new = sub_10097D094 @ 0x10097d094): alloc via the GC allocator, set ob_type=&PyInstanceMethod_Type(0x101a79c20), Py_INCREF(func), store func at method+0x10, then GC-track. Not exported (stripped exe) + single caller => standalone dead-stripped.
PyInstanceMethod_New.fallback: Capability preserved. PyInstanceMethod_Type is present/ready at 0x101a79c20 with tp_new=0x10097d094. Create a self-binding instancemethod by CALLING the type with your callable: PyObject_Call((PyObject*)0x101a79c20, one_tuple, NULL) or (once you have it) PyObject_CallFunctionObjArgs((PyObject*)0x101a79c20, callable, NULL). That runs tp_new (the inlined New) and returns an instancemethod whose tp_descr_get(0x10097d078) binds self on attribute access. Or call tp_new directly: ((PyObject*(*)(PyObject*,PyObject*,PyObject*))0x10097d094)(0x101a79c20, one_tuple, NULL). im->func @ +0x10, basicsize 0x18.

PyErr_Clear.evidence: No standalone tiny copy surfaced (consistent with PyErr_Occurred being inlined; stock 0xd0bd4 is a 5-instr tail-call to _PyErr_Restore(tstate,0,0,0)). Treat as inlined.
PyErr_Clear.equivalent: From frida: t=*(void**)0x101c0acd8; save old = t[0x58],t[0x60],t[0x68]; set them NULL; Py_XDECREF each old (decref = if(--*(ssize_t*)o==0) (*(void(**)(void*))(*(void**)((char*)o+8)+0x30))(o)). If you only need to *test/consume* errors, clearing the three fields to NULL (leaking a ref) is acceptable in a mod. A cleaner option is to locate _PyErr_Restore and call it with (tstate,0,0,0).
